findings.title: Slice design fully addresses the scope defined in architecture entry 915
findings.description: Every element the slice plan entry 915 requires is implemented: `scope: 'shared' | 'personal'` on `ConfigKeyDefinition`, project-level reads/writes routed inside `ConfigManager` per key classification, a second project file `.context-forge.local.toml`, `cf init`'s minimal gitignore addition, a full migration story for pre-existing personal keys committed to the shared file, and the explicit cross-package touch to `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/configTools.ts`. The `Explicitly excluded` list correctly respects the architecture's "Future Work" boundaries (broader gitignore scaffolding, auto-fix wiring).

findings.title: Three-tier precedence extends the "two-file-precedence merge pattern" mentioned in the slice plan
findings.description: Slice plan entry 915 says "reusing the existing user-vs-project two-file-precedence merge pattern rather than inventing a new one." The design introduces a three-tier precedence (`project-personal → project-shared → user → default`). This is a natural extension of the same precedence-based approach rather than a new mechanism (no switch statements, callbacks, or parallel paths), so it remains consistent with the architecture's intent — more specific scope wins. No action required; flagged only because the wording shifts from "two-file" to "three-tier."

findings.title: Read-path failure modes for the new personal file rely on inherited helper behavior without restating it
findings.description: Failure modes are enumerated for `migrate-personal`, `ConfigManager.set` writes, and `cf init`'s gitignore append. Read-path failures for `.context-forge.local.toml` (malformed TOML, permission denied, etc.) are not explicitly enumerated; the "same helper, same error path" rationale that justifies `set` writes also applies to reads, but the design states this only once (for writes). A one-sentence parallel statement for reads would close the gap. Minor observation — the inheritance argument is valid.

findings.title: Collision semantics and idempotency for `migrate-personal` are thoroughly specified
findings.description: The design explicitly handles three collision cases (absent-in-personal, present-with-different-value, present-with-identical-value) with per-key write-personal-then-delete-shared ordering and idempotent re-runnability. Failure between the two steps is reasoned through (recoverable via read-time fallback). The slice plan required "a defined migration/compat story"; the design exceeds that bar without over-engineering (e.g., no dry-run flag, no interactive confirmation beyond existing CLI conventions, as noted in `Implementation Notes > Special Considerations`).
